papers.title_en: Prevalence and Actionability of MTAP Loss in Driver Oncogene-Positive and Oncogene-Negative Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Sakai T, Piotrowska Z, Wang CI, Yeap BY, Sabbagh M, Heist RS, Lin JJ, Highfield LE et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Massachusetts General Hospital United States.
papers.authors_conclusion: MTAP缺失见于17%的NSCLC，包括24%的癌基因驱动肿瘤。PRMT5抑制剂活性不依赖于TKI暴露和SDMA表达，并由TKI治疗增强。这些发现支持在癌基因驱动的NSCLC中评估PRMT5抑制剂+TKI。
papers.ai_note: 驱动阳性与驱动阴性MTAP缺失率差异未达统计学显著（24% vs 14%，p=0.314），但结论仍以24%的癌基因驱动肿瘤表述作为核心卖点；'联合优于单药'及细胞系敏感性均为定性描述，摘要未给出IC50、抑制率或统计检验数值；'NGS会低估拷贝缺失'的立论在本研究中未做IHC与NGS的直接比对验证；结论从体外细胞系数据直接外推至支持临床联合用药评估，属转化证据的过度延伸
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: MTAP loss co-occurs with actionable genomic alterations in NSCLC and creates vulnerability to protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) inhibition. Estimates of prevalence of MTAP loss rely on next-generation sequencing which can underestimate copy losses. Moreover, the activity of PRMT5 inhibitors in oncogene-driven NSCLC is not well established. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: We assessed MTAP expression by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in 243 NSCLCs (n=132 early stage, n=111 metastatic), including 33 specimens with paired lymph nodes. Activity of PRMT5 inhibitor monotherapy and in combination with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) was evaluated in MTAP-deleted NSCLC cell lines harboring EGFR or KRAS mutations or ALK rearrangements. RESULTS: Among 243 NSCLC specimens from 240 patients (72% with driver alterations, 90% adenocarcinoma), MTAP loss was identified in 42 (17%) specimens, including 17 (13%) early-stage and 22 (20%) metastatic specimens. MTAP loss occurred in 24% of stage 4 driver-positive NSCLCs versus 14% of driver-negative tumors (p=0.314). Twenty-one (64%) lung-nodal pairs demonstrated concordance; eight cases only exhibited decreased MTAP expression in nodes. Variable sensitivity to PRMT5 inhibitors was observed in 22 MTAP-deleted NSCLC cell lines (9 EGFR-mutant, 7 KRAS-mutant, 6 ALK-rearranged), with responses seen in TKI-sensitive and TKI-resistant lines. SDMA (symmetric dimethylarginine) expression did not predict PRMT5 inhibitor sensitivity. TKI + PRMT5 inhibitor combos had greater activity than monotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: MTAP loss occurs in 17% of NSCLC, including 24% of oncogene-driven tumors. PRMT5 inhibitor activity is independent of TKI exposure and SDMA expression and enhanced by TKI therapy. These findings support evaluation of PRMT5 inhibitor + TKIs in oncogene-driven NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Background Lung cancer associated with cystic airspaces (CA) can be misinterpreted as a benign lesion, leading to missed or delayed diagnosis; however, the effect of the Lung Imaging Reporting and Data System (Lung-RADS) 2022 criteria remains unverified. Purpose To retrospectively determine the frequency and outcomes of lung cancer associated with CA during screening and explore the potential effect of Lung-RADS 2022 on earlier diagnosis. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis included participants with lung cancers from three trials: the National Lung Screening Trial (2002-2007); Italian Lung Cancer Screening Trial, or ITALUNG (2004-2010); and German Lung Cancer Screening Intervention trial, or LUSI (2007-2016). Two radiologists jointly reviewed low-dose CT images to identify and morphologically characterize lung cancer associated with CA. Associations with histologic features, stage, and other variables were assessed. Lung cancer-specific survival was analyzed using Fine-Gray regression accounting for the competing risk of non-lung cancer death. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, stage, detection status, and trial. Lung-RADS 2022 criteria for atypical pulmonary cysts were applied. Results Seventy-three cancers associated with CA were identified in 1258 participants (median age, 64 years [IQR, 61-69 years]; 43 male), including 44 of 716 (6.1%) screening-detected and 29 of 542 (5.4%) non-screening-detected cancers. Multilocular morphologic type was associated with a more advanced stage than unilocular morphologic type (12 of 24 vs 15 of 49; P = .02). The 5-year lung cancer-specific survival was 51.4% (95% CI: 39.3, 62.3) for cancers associated with CA and 53.2% (95% CI: 50.1, 56.2) for 1054 participants with noncystic non-small cell lung cancer. No evidence of a difference in survival was observed (subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.15 [95% CI: 0.81, 1.63]; P = .44), and results remained consistent in multivariable models. Lung-RADS 2022 might have enabled earlier diagnosis in 55 of 73 cancers associated with CA (75%). Conclusion Lung cancer associated with CA accounted for 6.1% of screening-detected and 5.4% of non-screening-detected lung cancers. Outcomes were similar to those of noncystic non-small cell lung cancer, and Lung-RADS 2022 may facilitate earlier diagnosis. Clinical trial registration nos. NCT00047385, NCT02777996, and ISRCTN N30604390 © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Byrne and Hammer in this issue.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurate characterization of pulmonary subsolid nodules (SSNs) is important for selecting surveillance, biopsy, or surgery. Existing clinical models were developed in broader nodule populations and may not fully reflect the radiological and biological features of SSNs. METHODS: This dual-center retrospective study included 225 patients with pathologically confirmed SSNs from January 2018 to January 2024. The development center contributed 167 patients, split into internal training (n = 118) and internal validation (n = 49) cohorts, and the external center contributed 58 patients. Ten machine-learning algorithms were compared within the development cohort. The final combined model used four routinely available predictors: spiculation, consolidation-to-tumor ratio (CTR), CYFRA 21 - 1, and nodule diameter. Discrimination, calibration, decision-curve analysis, pairwise model comparison, and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.932 (95% CI, 0.887-0.977), 0.954 (95% CI, 0.895-1.000), and 0.930 (95% CI, 0.864-0.995) in the internal training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. In external validation, the corresponding AUCs for the Mayo, VA, Brock, and PKUPH models were 0.750, 0.560, 0.800, and 0.840. Calibration was evaluated in all three cohorts, and decision-curve analysis showed net benefit across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.12-0.68 in external validation. CONCLUSIONS: A four-variable combined model integrating imaging features and CYFRA 21 - 1 showed consistent discrimination across the internal and external validation cohorts. The web calculator may support research-stage risk estimation, but prospective multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract_en: Early lung adenocarcinoma presenting as ground-glass nodules (GGNs) is increasingly detected in clinical practice. However, robust biomarkers reflecting progression from in situ to invasive disease are incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, T-cell receptor repertoire profiling, whole-slide immunohistochemistry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, and an orthotopic murine lung adenocarcinoma model to dissect the immune landscape of primary GGNs. We found that these early thoracic lesions harbored abundant infiltrates of innate and adaptive immune cells, but intratumoral T lymphocytes included putative polyclonal bystander clones embedded in an immunosuppressive microenvironment. We further observed a marked stage-dependent increase in T and B cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), dominated by immature configurations, whereas mature TLSs remained relatively infrequent. In mouse allografts, spontaneously arising TLSs were likewise underdeveloped, and LTαβ or LIGHT overexpression, as well as PD-1 blockade, promoted TLS neogenesis and maturation, accompanied by reduced tumor growth. Collectively, our study delineates the immunologic features associated with pathological invasion, identifies a predominance of structurally immature TLS niches, and provides a rationale for further investigating the therapeutic potential of promoting TLS maturation to intercept early lung adenocarcinoma.

papers.abstract_en: Recent clinical trials show prominent anti-tumor activity of CD73-blocking antibodies in combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) antagonists in a subset of patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which highlights the need to understand the properties of the CD39/CD73 pathway in human lung malignancies and its modulation by other anti-cancer therapies. To address this, we study the distribution, biological context, spatial heterogeneity, clinical significance, and modulation of CD39/CD73 using multiplexed quantitative immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics analysis of multiple NSCLC patient cohorts, as well as in vitro experiments of cultured NSCLC cells. Our results reveal an asymmetric distribution of the CD39/CD73 pathway within the tumor microenvironment, preferential expression in lung adenocarcinomas with elevated PD-L1 and effector T cell infiltration or lacking STK11/KEAP1 mutations, limited intratumor spatial heterogeneity, and differential modulation of cancer cell CD73 by proinflammatory cytokines and systemic radio-chemotherapy. Collectively, our results can inform optimal design of therapeutic interventions and patient selection strategies.

papers.title_en: Patterns of Treatment and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Stage 1/2 EGFR-mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Treated With Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy: A Global, Multicenter, Retrospective Study.
papers.authors: Lin SH, Okishio K, Mizutani H, Lee JB, Kim SW, Smith D, Neal JW, Hochmair M et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Thoracic Radiation Oncology, MD Anderson Cancer Center, Houston, Texas, USA.
papers.authors_conclusion: 在这一全球、真实世界、回顾性的I/II期EGFR突变NSCLC接受SBRT（多数为医学不可手术）的研究中，4年rwPFS率<50%。需要进一步研究以确认EGFR-TKI治疗在此场景中的潜在作用。
papers.ai_note: 样本量小（n=82）、无对照组，无法区分SBRT疗效与疾病自然史及后续TKI的贡献；主要终点rwPFS为真实世界指标，疾病进展判定标准未在摘要中说明，可能存在评估异质性；后续接受TKI治疗者仅25例且一代/二代为主（17例），三代仅5例，据此提出TKI潜在作用的结论外推依据不足；60个月rwPFS的95%CI（19-48）很宽，估计不稳定；信息不足（摘要未报告分期/突变亚组的分层生存数据）。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: We report clinical outcomes, mutation testing patterns, and treatment patterns from a global, real-world, retrospective, observational study in patients with stage 1/2 epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). METHODS AND MATERIALS: Data were extracted from medical records of adults with stage 1/2 EGFR-mutated NSCLC (diagnosed January 2016-December 2019), who underwent stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) as standard of care. The primary objective was assessment of real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS). Secondary objectives included assessment of mutation testing patterns, treatment sequencing post-SBRT, real-world time to next treatment or death (rwTTNTD), and real-world overall survival (rwOS). RESULTS: Data were extracted from medical records of 82 patients across six countries; 66% of patients had medically inoperable tumors; 43% had tumors harboring exon 19 deletion (Ex19del), 55% had L858R, 1% had both Ex19del and L858R, and 1% had L858R and an exon 20 insertion. Overall, 91% of patients had stage 1A/1B disease and 9% had stage 2A/2B. All patients underwent SBRT as standard of care; 31 patients (38%) progressed following SBRT. Of patients who received subsequent treatment (n = 25), most received EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs; 88%; n = 22/25); first-/second-generation EGFR-TKIs n=17, third-generation EGFR-TKIs n=5. Median (95% confidence interval [CI]) rwPFS, rwTTNTD, and rwOS were 47.1 (38.7-57.8), 49.8 (40.7-not estimable [NE]), and 62.9 (50.8-NE) months, respectively. The rwPFS rates at 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months (95% CI) were 90% (81-95), 76% (65-84), 65% (53-74), 48% (35-60), and 34% (19-48), respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In this global, real-world, retrospective study in patients with stage 1/2 EGFR-mutated NSCLC who underwent SBRT, the majority of whom had medically inoperable tumors, the 4-year rwPFS rate was <50%. Further studies are needed to confirm the potential role for EGFR-TKI therapy in this setting.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of pulmonary rehabilitation exercise on postoperative quality of life (QoL) and symptom cluster (pain, fatigue, shortness of breath) in lung cancer survivors, meanwhile, to explore the interrelationships among these symptoms. METHODS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were retrieved from six databases. Pooled standardized mean difference (SMD) was calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup analyses stratified by intervention duration, multiple sensitivity tests and trim-and-fill analysis were performed. Study-level correlation and regression analyses investigated symptom associations. Evidence certainty was assessed via GRADE. RESULTS: Ten RCTs with 852 participants were included. Perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation modestly improved QoL (standardized mean difference [SMD] = 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.23 to 1.58), 6-minute walk distance (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI 0.00 to 0.43) and full vital capacity (SMD = 1.16; 95% CI 0.44 to 1.89), and alleviated the postoperative symptom cluster (pain (SMD = -0.49; 95% CI -0.92 to -0.07), fatigue (SMD = -0.65; 95% CI -0.87 to -0.42) and shortness of breath (SMD = -0.71; 95% CI -1.10 to -0.32)). Moderate-to-strong positive pairwise correlations were detected among symptoms, with pain identified as the core correlated symptom within the symptom cluster. CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative pulmonary rehabilitation may improve functional recovery and relieve postoperative symptoms in lung cancer patients. Preoperative intervention and structured rehabilitation lasting at least two months are worthy of attention. As substantial heterogeneity and limited evidence certainty exist, conclusions should be interpreted cautiously. Large standardized RCTs are required to confirm optimal rehabilitation protocols.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The da Vinci single-port (SP) robotic system was approved for thoracic surgery in the United States in July 2024. Reports of its application in lung cancer remain limited. We present the initial experience with 145 consecutive SP resections for primary lung cancer at a single institution, with an emphasis on safety and oncologic quality. DESCRIPTION: The SP robotic platform enables lung resection through a single subcostal incision, avoiding intercostal nerve injury. EVALUATION: Three surgeons performed 34 SP lobectomies, 23 segmentectomies, and 88 wedge resections (95% stage I, 5% post-induction) between 6/2025-7/2026. Perioperative outcomes, oncologic quality, and learning curve were analyzed. Median operative time was 113 minutes, estimated blood loss 10mL, and length of stay 2 days. There were 3 conversions. R0 resection occurred in 99.3% of cases. Median lymph node yield was 5 nodes. There were zero mortalities and 4.8% major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥III). Cumulative-sum analysis identified a learning curve plateau after 23 cases. CONCLUSIONS: Subcostal SP robotic lung resection is feasible and safe with acceptable perioperative and oncologic outcomes. Comparative studies are warranted.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether serial quantitative computed tomography (CT) volume change is associated with mortality, acute exacerbation, and concurrent pulmonary function decline in fibrotic interstitial lung disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 102 participants who underwent surgical lung biopsy and paired CT between October 2018 and August 2023. A deep learning-based quantitative CT system measured fibrotic lesion and normal-lung volumes. Spearman correlations compared CT measures. Cox models assessed baseline volumes and annualized changes; linear models assessed concurrent pulmonary function change. RESULTS: Median age was 65 years [interquartile range, 56-69]; 68 participants were men. During median 4.82 years of follow-up, 12 deaths and 15 acute exacerbations occurred. Fibrotic lesion and normal-lung volumes were inversely correlated at baseline and follow-up, as were their annualized changes (ρ = -0.53, - 0.60, and - 0.56, respectively). Annualized fibrotic lesion volume increase (hazard ratio per 100 mL/year, 1.40; 95% confidence interval 1.15-1.69; q = 0.0036) and annualized normal-lung volume loss (hazard ratio per 500 mL/year decrease, 1.57; 95% confidence interval 1.20-2.06; q = 0.0036) were associated with death. Baseline fibrotic lesion volume was associated with acute exacerbation (hazard ratio per 100 mL, 1.33; 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.63; q = 0.012). Greater fibrotic lesion increase and normal-lung loss were associated with forced vital capacity decline; diffusing capacity associations were not significant after correction. CONCLUSION: Serial quantitative CT volume change was associated with mortality and concurrent forced vital capacity decline, whereas baseline fibrotic lesion burden was associated with acute exacerbation in fibrotic interstitial lung disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of mortality, yet early detection remains challenging. This study assessed whether deep learning applied to routine outpatient chest radiographs (CXRs) can identify individuals at high risk of incident COPD. METHODS: Using cancer screening trial data, we previously developed a convolutional neural network (CXR-Lung-Risk) to predict lung-related mortality from a CXR image. In this retrospective model validation study, we externally validated whether CXR-Lung-Risk was associated with incident COPD from routine CXRs. We identified outpatients without lung cancer, COPD, or emphysema who had a CXR taken from Jan 1, 2013, to Dec 31, 2014, at Massachusetts General or Brigham and Women's Hospitals in Boston, MA, USA. The primary outcome was 6-year incident COPD. Discrimination was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) compared with the TargetCOPD clinical risk score. All analyses were stratified by smoking status. A secondary analysis was conducted in the Project Baseline Health Study (PBHS) to test associations between CXR-Lung-Risk with pulmonary function and plasma protein abundance. The PBHS study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03154346. FINDINGS: The primary analysis consisted of data from 12 550 ever-smokers (mean age 62·4 years [SD 6·8], 6135 [48·9%] male, 6415 [51·1%] female) and 15 298 never-smokers (mean age 63·0 years [8·1], 6550 [42·8%] male, 8748 [57·2%] female). 1562 (12·4%) of 12 550 ever-smokers and 580 (3·8%) of 15 298 never-smokers developed COPD within 6 years. CXR-Lung-Risk had additive predictive value beyond the TargetCOPD score for 6-year incident COPD in both ever-smokers (CXR-Lung-Risk + TargetCOPD AUC 0·73 [95% CI 0·72-0·74] vs TargetCOPD alone AUC 0·66 [0·65-0·68], p<0·0001) and never-smokers (CXR-Lung-Risk + TargetCOPD AUC 0·70 [0·67-0·72] vs TargetCOPD alone AUC 0·60 [0·57-0·62], p<0·0001). In secondary analyses of 2097 individuals in the PBHS, CXR-Lung-Risk was associated with worse pulmonary function and with abundance of SCGB3A2 (secretoglobin family 3A member 2) and LYZ (lysozyme), proteins involved in pulmonary physiology. INTERPRETATION: In this external validation, a deep-learning model applied to routine CXR images identified individuals at high risk of incident COPD, beyond known risk factors. Patients at high risk might benefit from diagnostic spirometry and subsequent preventive care. FUNDING: Verily Life Sciences, San Francisco, California.

papers.title_en: Microbial ecological instability and non-linear host interactions shape airway inflammation in HIV-associated COPD.
papers.authors: Kayongo A, Bartolomaeus TUP, Hecker J, Birkner T, Vila E, Ntayi ML, Markó L, Löber U et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Immunology and Molecular Biology, Makerere University College of Health Sciences, Kampala, Uganda.
papers.authors_conclusion: We find that sputum microbial communities are shaped predominantly by temporal ecological turnover rather than HIV or COPD status. Although microbial diversity, microbiome instability, outer membrane vesicle burden and inferred airway cellular composition remain largely preserved, HIV-associated COPD exhibits disease-specific microbial signatures together with inflammatory transcriptional remodeling concentrated in induced sputum. Integrated analyses identify selective host-microbe interaction networks linking discrete microbial taxa with inflammatory, immune and transcriptional programmes.
papers.ai_note: 标题称'Microbial ecological instability ... shape airway inflammation'，但摘要正文明确写 microbiome instability 'remain largely preserved'，标题与主要发现存在矛盾，且标题暗示的因果性（shape）超出观察性设计可支持的范围。摘要全文未报告任何效应量、置信区间或P值，无法判断'病原特异性菌群特征'与'选择性宿主-微生物互作网络'的统计强度与多重比较校正情况；'非线性'互作的建模方法与验证方式信息不足。同时摘要强调时间性生态演替是菌群变异的主导因素、多样性与不稳定性大体保留，这一偏阴性的主干发现未在标题中体现。
papers.abstract_en: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized among people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, yet the mechanisms linking airway microbial ecology to chronic inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we study 200 adults stratified by HIV and COPD status, including 160 participants with two-year longitudinal follow-up, using an integrated multi-omics framework combining sputum 16S rRNA profiling, bacterial outer membrane vesicle quantification, airway cytokine profiling, CyTOF immune phenotyping, bulk transcriptomics of induced sputum, bronchoalveolar lavage and peripheral blood, and bronchoalveolar lavage single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution. We find that sputum microbial communities are shaped predominantly by temporal ecological turnover rather than HIV or COPD status. Although microbial diversity, microbiome instability, outer membrane vesicle burden and inferred airway cellular composition remain largely preserved, HIV-associated COPD exhibits disease-specific microbial signatures together with inflammatory transcriptional remodeling concentrated in induced sputum. Integrated analyses identify selective host-microbe interaction networks linking discrete microbial taxa with inflammatory, immune and transcriptional programmes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Nighttime admission to the intensive care unit (ICU) has been associated with worse outcomes in some critically ill populations. However, evidence specific to patients with severe pneumonia is limited. We evaluated the association between ICU admission time and 30-day mortality among patients with severe pneumonia requiring invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with ICD-coded severe pneumonia who received IMV in four campuses at a tertiary medical center between 2020 and 2024. Patients were categorized according to their ICU admission time and our institutional staffing schedule: daytime admission (08:00-15:59) and nighttime admission (16:00-07:59 the following day). The primary outcome was 30-day mortality after ICU admission. Survival analysis and multivariable Cox regression were used to test the association between admission time and 30-day mortality. RESULTS: A total of 9,611 patients were included in the analysis. Among them, 6,058 patients were admitted at night, and 3,553 during the daytime. After 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM), 3,476 patients remained in each group. There was no statistically significant difference in 30-day mortality following ICU admission between the two groups (hazard ratio [HR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.92-1.09; P = 0.914). After adjustment for age, sex, relative weight, lactate, patient source, type of admission, and septic shock, multivariable Cox regression showed that daytime ICU admission was not an independent protective factor for 30-day mortality (adjusted HR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.93-1.10; P = 0.794). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of patients with severe pneumonia requiring IMV, ICU admission timing was not significantly associated with 30-day mortality. The findings should be interpreted in light of residual confounding and the institution-specific staffing model.

papers.authors: Sayed MS, Gebaly DM, Ilyas H, Abdelhamed R, Rasheed WM, Hamdy H, Melad L, Andò G et al.

papers.ai_note: 主要终点全因死亡点估计RR 0.88方向有利于CDT、CI上限1.01且p=0.068接近显著，摘要以'无差异'定性，属边界结果而非确证等效；未报告异质性（I²）、研究质量评价与发表偏倚评估，观察性研究占主导时残余混杂（病情严重度、器械选择偏倚）可同时影响死亡与ICU时长；'中/高危'混合人群未按风险分层或按CTEPH/血流动力学状态亚组拆分；ICU住院时长差异1.01天的临床意义未讨论；检索截止2026年6月与本研究其他信息核对需注意时间一致性。信息不足：未给出各研究设计构成比例与敏感性分析结果。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model. RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups. CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute respiratory infections (ARI), yet evidence from outpatient settings, particularly among older adults, remains limited. METHODS: BUCOSS was a prospective observational study conducted across three consecutive respiratory seasons (2022-2025) in patients aged ≥ 60 years with ARI, recruited from 29 primary care and office-based pulmonology practices. RSV and other respiratory pathogens were identified via multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of nasopharyngeal swabs. RSV-positive patients were followed for 28 days to assess symptom burden, complications and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). RESULTS: RSV had a prevalence of 5.49% (95% CI: 2.96-8.03) and an incidence of 1,030.63/100,000 (95% CI: 824.48-1,287.66). Among 3,261 patients with ARI, 192 (5.9%) tested positive for RSV. The mean age of RSV-infected individuals was 71.6 years; 90.6% had at least one comorbidity. RSV infection was associated with a significantly higher burden of lower respiratory tract symptoms - notably cough, sputum production and wheezing - compared with other viral ARI, whereas systemic symptoms such as fever and myalgia were less prominent. Within 28 days, 30% of RSV-positive patients developed complications, predominantly pulmonary. Chronic lung disease (RR1.62 (0.95; 2.77)) and the presence of lower respiratory tract symptoms at presentation (RR 1.78 (0.92; 3.45)) trended to be independently associated with increased complication risk. CONCLUSION: RSV constitutes a substantial cause of ARI in older, multimorbid outpatients, distinguished by a pronounced lower respiratory tract symptom profile and a high rate of pulmonary complications. These findings underscore the need for targeted prevention strategies and tailored clinical management in high-risk adult populations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Brazilian data on the course of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) after a myocardial infarction or stroke are scarce. OBJECTIVES: To estimate the association of myocardial infarction or stroke with death and hospital resource use in patients with COPD in a Brazilian private healthcare network. METHODS: Retrospective cohort of patients aged 40 years or older with a COPD-specific ICD-10 code (J41 to J44) and a spirometry report, followed from the date both criteria were met. Myocardial infarction or stroke was a time-varying exposure: patients with a history at entry were exposed from entry, and those with a first event during follow-up were exposed from the event. Cox models with the time-varying exposure and negative binomial regression were used. RESULTS: The 1,257 patients were followed for 1,368 person-years; 63 had a history of myocardial infarction or stroke at entry and 41 had a first event during follow-up. Sixty-two died, 3.8 per 100 person-years in unexposed and 15.4 in exposed person-time (adjusted HR 3.81; 95% CI 2.00 to 7.27; p < 0.001), with the highest hazard in the first 90 days after an incident event (HR 4.26). Exposed person-time had more hospital admissions (IRR 2.69; 95% CI 1.85 to 3.92) and intensive care unit admissions (IRR 3.77; 95% CI 2.25 to 6.33). CONCLUSION: In patients with COPD, myocardial infarction or stroke was followed by a near fourfold increase in the hazard of death and a threefold increase in hospital admissions.

papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Biomedical Engineering, Guangzhou Medical University, Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.
papers.authors_conclusion: Collectively, this study identifies the MAPK-mitochondrial metabolic axis as a critical regulator of hypoxia-induced NK cell dysfunction and proposes metabolic preconditioning as a strategy to overcome solid tumor hypoxia.
papers.ai_note: 信息不足：摘要通篇为定性描述（'significantly impairs'、'remarkably restores'），未报告任何效应量、样本量、统计学检验或CI/P，无法评估效应大小与可靠性；主要终点未预先界定，转录组学提示MAPK通路后以'常氧下MAPK抑制模拟HPC保护'作功能验证，属机制性衔接而非独立终点；结论外推至人iNK细胞仅一句'supports broader evaluation'，缺乏人体数据；临床转化可行性（预处理方案在患者中的实施）未涉及。
papers.abstract_en: Solid tumor hypoxia is a major barrier to NK cell-based immunotherapy. To address this challenge, we establish a hypoxic preconditioning (HPC) model. We find that acute hypoxia (AH; 1% O2) significantly impairs NK92 cell cytotoxicity-such as granzyme B secretion and infiltration into lung cancer cell spheroids. In contrast, HPC pretreatment (gradual reduction from 5% to 1% O2) remarkably restores these functions. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis reveals that HPC markedly attenuates hypoxia -induced aberrant MAPK pathway activation. MAPK attenuation under normoxia recapitulates HPC -like protection by promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic remodeling, thereby enhancing the antitumor activity of NK92 cells both in vitro and in vivo. Notably, systemic MAPK inhibitor injection increases NKp46 expression on endogenous NK cells in BALB/c mice. Importantly, this strategy is also effective in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived induced NK (iNK) cells, supporting broader evaluation across NK cell platforms. Collectively, this study identifies the MAPK-mitochondrial metabolic axis as a critical regulator of hypoxia-induced NK cell dysfunction and proposes metabolic preconditioning as a strategy to overcome solid tumor hypoxia.

papers.abstract_en: Evaluate differences in operative cost in pulmonary resection between patients who had preoperative biopsy via robotic navigational bronchoscopy versus an intraoperative diagnostic wedge. We performed a retrospective cohort study of patients who underwent standard lobectomy at our institution between January 2024 and July 2025. We identified patients who had a preoperative robotic navigational bronchoscopy (Nav) prior to lung resection and those who had no preoperative biopsy (NPB) and had intraoperative diagnostic wedge. We then examined operative time, stapler load quantity, stapler cost, robotic cost, and overall operative cost. 128 patients were identified, 53 in the NPB cohort and 75 in the Nav cohort. The mean age of the cohort was 68. The average surgical cost of the non-preoperative biopsy (NPB) cohort was $10,258.68 and $9,249.36 in the Nav cohort (P = 0.007). The average stapler loads used, total stapler cost, total robotic I&A costs, and surgical supply costs were higher in the NPB cohort (P < 0.001). The average technical cost of performing a frozen specimen was $65.35. There was no statistically significant difference in operative time between cohorts, however the NPB cohort had a longer operative time on average (187.83 min vs. 174.63 min, P = 0.161). We found that on average, surgical cost, operative time, robotic cost, and OR charges were higher in patients who had undergone intraoperative frozen section (NPB) compared to those with preoperative biopsy (Nav). This data suggest that the use of preoperative robotic bronchoscopy is associated with decreased cost of robotic lung resection.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Lung cancer screening has improved early detection among individuals who meet established age and smoking criteria. However, many patients who develop lung cancer remain ineligible for screening. Incidental pulmonary nodules (ILN) identified on imaging performed for other indications may provide important complementary pathway for early lung cancer detection, but the contribution of structured ILN programs to cancer detection outside conventional screening eligibility remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from two urban academic hospitals from January 2023 through January 4, 2026. Patients with ILN requiring surveillance were identified using natural language processing of radiology reports and navigator review. Screening eligibility was classified according to 2021 United States Preventive Services Task Force criteria. Cancer detection, stage, histology, treatment, and factors associated with cancer among screening-ineligible patients were evaluated. RESULTS: Among 2,804 patients requiring follow-up, 2,248 (80.2 %) were screening ineligible, 466 (16.6 %) eligible, and 90 (3.2 %) unclassified. Lung cancer was diagnosed in 73 patients (2.6 %), including 44 (60.3 %) who were screening ineligible. Of these, 15 were never-smokers and 29 were former or current smokers who did not meet screening criteria. Thirty-six (81.8 %) had stage 0-II disease, 21 (47.7 %) underwent definitive surgical resection, and 36 (81.8 %) had adenocarcinoma. Nodule diameter > 8 mm was associated with lung cancer diagnosis (adjusted odds ratio 15.89; 95 % CI 5.24-71.47). CONCLUSIONS: The ILN program identified substantial early-stage, clinically actionable lung cancers among patients outside conventional screening eligibility. The high proportion of early-stage diagnoses and definitive resections supports ILN programs as a complementary pathway to organized lung cancer screening.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) is a severe type 2 inflammatory airway disease caused by hypersensitivity to Aspergillus fumigatus. Although omalizumab has been used as an adjunctive therapy for ABPA, longitudinal changes in type 2 inflammatory and Aspergillus-specific biomarkers during treatment remain incompletely characterized. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate clinical outcomes and longitudinal biomarker changes during omalizumab therapy in patients with ABPA. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 15 adults with ABPA treated with omalizumab 600 mg every 4 weeks and followed for 36 weeks. Clinical outcomes, including pulmonary function, fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO), blood eosinophil counts, and oral corticosteroid (OCS) use, were assessed at baseline, week 12, and week 36. Serial measurements of total IgE, A. fumigatus-specific IgE and IgG4, thymus and activation-regulated chemokine (TARC/CCL17), IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 were performed. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using the Friedman test, with false discovery rate (FDR)-adjusted q values calculated for multiple testing. RESULTS: Omalizumab treatment was associated with reductions in OCS dose, FeNO, blood eosinophils, TARC, IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 (all overall P<0.001, FDR q<0.001). Median OCS dose decreased from 15.0 to 0 mg/day, FeNO from 43.0 to 22.0 ppb, and eosinophils from 0.58 to 0.06 ×109/L by week 36. Individual trajectories were predominantly downward, with monotonic declines in 80.0%-100% of participants depending on the marker. PEF increased significantly, whereas the increase in FEV1 was not statistically significant. A. fumigatus-specific IgE and IgG4 declined, while total IgE showed no sustained decrease. No significant associations were detected between total IgE and TARC or the measured cytokines (all nominal P≥0.062; all FDR q≥0.482). No serious treatment-related adverse events were observed. CONCLUSION: In this real-world ABPA cohort, omalizumab therapy was associated with corticosteroid reduction and parallel declines in several type 2-associated biomarkers over 36 weeks. These longitudinal clinical and biomarker profiles provide a more detailed picture of treatment-associated changes and a basis for prospective evaluation of their clinical relevance.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Tarlatamab has demonstrated activity in relapsed small cell lung cancer (SCLC). However, lesion-level response heterogeneity and organ-specific patterns of progression during tarlatamab therapy remain poorly characterized in clinical practice. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients with relapsed SCLC treated with tarlatamab between June 2021 and March 2026. Overall response at the first radiological evaluation and best overall response were assessed according to the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version 1.1. Lesion-level response patterns at the first radiological assessment were categorized as responsive, mixed response, stable, or progressive. Progression sites, intracranial lesion changes, and progression-free survival (PFS) were analyzed. Site-specific findings were summarized at the first evaluation and at overall progressive disease (PD). RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were included. Mixed response was observed in 11 (37.9%) patients and across the RECIST response categories at the first radiological evaluation. The median PFS was 3.2 months and was longest in the responsive group, intermediate in the mixed-response group, and shortest in the progressive group. Among 15 patients evaluable for intracranial response, seven experienced at least 30% intracranial tumor shrinkage at the first assessment, and four subsequently developed intracranial progression. Among 20 patients with disease progression, 12 had progression at three or more sites. Site-specific assessments showed that decreased or stable disease could coexist with overall PD. CONCLUSION: Tarlatamab showed heterogeneous response and progression patterns in relapsed SCLC, including frequent mixed response and intracranial progression. Lesion-level assessment may provide a more comprehensive characterization of disease behavior during tarlatamab therapy.

papers.abstract_en: A 64-year-old man who underwent bilateral orthotopic lung transplant for emphysema related to α1-antitrypsin deficiency 8 months ago presented to the clinic for assessment of bilateral pulmonary nodules identified on routine postlung transplant surveillance without any symptomatic concerns. The donor was positive for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus, and the recipient was negative for cytomegalovirus and positive for Epstein-Barr virus. He denied any fever, chills, cough, chest pain, dyspnea, weight loss, or night sweats. The patient lived in South Florida with no recent travel history outside the United States or infectious contacts. His posttransplant course was complicated with antibody-mediated rejection at 1.5 months after lung transplant. Antibody-mediated rejection was successfully treated with our institutional multimodal regimen, including a combination of plasmapheresis, carfilzomib, and anti-thymocyte globulin followed by monthly IV immunoglobulin and tocilizumab injections. Also, because of calcineurin inhibitor (CNI)-related renal dysfunction, the patient's immunosuppression was converted to a belatacept-based CNI-sparing regimen in addition to prednisone, with a tacrolimus goal trough of 4 to 6 ng/mL. He was also placed on mycophenolic acid, which was soon held because of neutropenia.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE: The large and growing burden of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) requires evidence-based policies to improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. We developed the Evaluation Platform in COPD in the U.S. (EPIC-US), a whole-disease model of COPD capable of evaluating interventions across all stages of disease progression within a single policy platform. OBJECTIVES: The objectives were to develop EPIC-US by adapting a model version developed for Canada (EPIC) and internally and externally validate EPIC-US to an independent clinical cohort. METHODS: EPIC-US is a stochastic discrete-event simulation model of COPD for U.S. individuals aged ≥40 years. It simulates COPD progression based on individualized trajectories of lung function decline and exacerbations. We matched population size to U.S. census projections for 2015-2060. All-cause mortality was taken from U.S. life tables. Historical and projected trends in tobacco smoking prevalence were aligned with 2018 and 2023 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) results, while COPD prevalence was informed by National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data. We used clinical trials, meta-analyses and U.S. administrative data to inform the rate and severity of exacerbations. We externally validated moderate exacerbations and severe exacerbations using the U.S. sub-sample of the NOVEL observational longiTudinal studY (NOVELTY). RESULTS: EPIC-US simulated outputs closely matched module-specific internal validation targets. The predicted population size of ≥ 40-year-olds was within 1-2% of U.S. Census projections. Predicted mean COPD prevalence (8.1% for ages 40-59 years; 14.4% for ages 60-79 years), and smoking prevalence in 2018 (12.9%) and 2023 (10.1%) were within 0.1-0.4% of NHIS and NHANES estimates. In 2016, EPIC-US predicted 560 hospitalizations for COPD per 100,000 person-years, consistent with the observed rate of 510 hospitalizations. In external validation, severe exacerbations rates in EPIC-US (0.039; 95% CI 0.035-0.043 per patient-year) were comparable to NOVELTY (0.022 per patient-year, 95% CI 0.008-0.065). EPIC-US replicated differences in exacerbation rate across classes of inhaled therapies. However, EPIC-US overpredicted the rate of moderate exacerbations relative to NOVELTY. CONCLUSION: EPIC-US is the first multi-purpose, whole-disease model of COPD in the U.S., providing a policy-ready platform for simulating both the clinical and economic burden of the disease.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative recovery after lung cancer surgery may be influenced by age, comorbidity burden, and perioperative rehabilitation strategies. However, evidence regarding the age-related effects of structured early inpatient physiotherapy programs remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the age-related effects of a comprehensive in patient physiotherapy (CIPT) program on hospital length of stay (LoS), clinical parameters, symptom-related outcomes, and inflammatory biomarkers in patients undergoing lung cancer surgery. METHODS: This ambispective observational cohort study included patients who underwent lung cancer surgery and received a structured CIPT program during the postoperative inpatient period as part of standard postoperative care. Participants were categorized into middle-aged and older groups. Outcomes included hospital LoS, clinical parameters (blood pressure, resting heart rate, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate), symptom-related outcomes (dyspnea and fatigue with Modified Borg Scale, and incisional pain with Visual analog scale), and inflammatory biomarkers (C-reactive protein (CRP), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and albumin). Pre- and post-program changes within groups and differences between age groups were analyzed. RESULTS: Median LoS was 7 [5-10] days in the middle-aged group and 7 [6-10] days in the older group, with no significant difference between groups. Significant improvements in resting heart rate, oxygen saturation, and dyspnea were observed in the older group, whereas dyspnea, fatigue, and incisional pain improved significantly in the middle-aged group. No significant differences were detected between age groups in clinical parameters or symptom-related outcomes. CRP and NLR levels decreased significantly in both groups, while albumin showed a non-significant upward trend over time. Despite a higher comorbidity burden in the older group, no adverse events or clinical instability were observed during the rehabilitation program. CONCLUSION: The CIPT program appears to be safe and feasible for both middle-aged and older patients following lung cancer surgery. Similar outcomes between age groups suggest that age alone may not represent a barrier to participation in structured early inpatient rehabilitation programs. Early physiotherapy integrated into postoperative care pathways may facilitate recovery without increasing hospital length of stay across age groups, which may also help reduce the potential economic burden associated with prolonged hospitalization. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Intraoperative augmented reality (AR) guidance could improve surgical orientation in robot-assisted minimally invasive esophagectomy (RAMIE), but reliable image-to-patient registration between preoperative imaging and the intraoperative scene remains a key technical barrier. This feasibility study aimed to explore the potential of AR for RAMIE and to establish a foundation for intraoperative AR guidance by systematically comparing image-to-patient registration methods using real-world clinical data. METHODS: In this feasibility study, ten consecutive patients undergoing RAMIE were included. Preoperative 3D anatomical models were generated from CT scans using semi-automated segmentation. Intraoperative 3D point clouds were reconstructed from stereoscopic robotic surgical video using stereo-based depth estimation. One manual and six fully automated image-to-patient registration methods were evaluated: Go-ICP, AFWA, CPD, RANSAC, Super4PCS, and FMR. The azygos vein was used as the registration landmark, and registration performance was assessed by qualitative acceptance rate and surface-to-surface distance using the trachea as an independent evaluation structure. RESULTS: Manual registration achieved a success rate of 0.80, with a mean surface distance (MSD) of 11.46 mm, Hausdorff distance (HD) of 15.20 mm, and a mean computation time of 22.73 s. Among automated methods, success rates ranged from 0.10 (AFWA, FMR) to 0.40 (Super4PCS). All automated methods completed registration in under 3 s. Surface distances were based on one to eight accepted registrations per method and did not reliably distinguish accepted from rejected registrations. CONCLUSION: This feasibility study shows that image-to-patient registration for augmented reality in RAMIE is technically achievable using real clinical data. Manual registration provides the highest robustness, while fully automated global methods remain limited under intraoperative conditions. Achieved registration accuracies in accepted cases may support basic anatomical orientation but require further development, particularly in deformable registration and intraoperative reconstruction, before reliable intraoperative AR guidance becomes feasible.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects cognitive performance and may contribute to long-term cognitive decline. Longitudinal assessments are needed for measuring changes in cognitive functioning in relation to OSA progression and treatment. This requires standardized, reliable cognitive assessments suitable for repeated use, but the psychometric properties of cognitive tests may vary across populations. We evaluated the suitability of a digital cognitive battery, covering various cognitive functions, for repeated administration in individuals with varying OSA severity, based on its psychometric properties. METHODS: The battery included 14 cognitive tasks. We assessed test-retest reliability, practice effects, and ceiling and floor effects between two administrations (mean interval 12 weeks) in 46 participants (mean age = 49 ± 16 years, 21 women) with a wide range of OSA severity (mean apnea-hypopnea-index (AHI) = 17.6 ± 17.7). RESULTS: Psychometric properties varied considerably between cognitive tasks. Test-retest reliability estimates were good or satisfactory (ICC≥.60) for the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT), Symbol Digit Modalities Task (SDMT), Paced Auditory Serial Addition Task (PASAT), Auditory Verbal Learning Task (AVLT), and subscores of the Tower of London Task (ToL). Practice effects were high for the PASAT in Level 1 (p<.001,r=.63) and the Inspection Time Task (ITT; p<.001,r=.52). Ceiling effects were present in the ITT and ToL, whereas intrusions in the AVLT and lapses in the PVT occurred infrequently and clustered at the lower bound. CONCLUSION: Only a subset of cognitive tasks showed adequate psychometrics for repeated administration, highlighting the need for careful task selection and modification when developing cognitive assessments for repeated application in OSA populations. We include recommendations on cognitive test selection and test design for repeated assessments in OSA populations.

papers.abstract_en: Thymoma is the most common anterior mediastinal tumor, which is linked to the loss of self-tolerance and the presence of autoimmunity. Various interactions between thymoma and autoimmune diseases have been identified, including myasthenia gravis, systemic lupus erythematosus, pure red cell aplasia, and pemphigus. In this retrospective case series, we reported rare autoimmune disorders with different organ involvement associated with thymoma. These included ocular paraneoplastic pemphigus, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, diffuse panbronchiolitis and myositis. Our series broadens the spectrum of autoimmune disorders with shared T cell-mediated and B cell-dependent pathogenesis, underscoring the recurrence or relapse of thymoma-associated autoimmunity. The recognition of rare autoimmune presentations charts future treatment decisions and multidisciplinary care.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Otorhinolaryngology, St Luke's Hospital, Bystrzanska 94 B, 43-309, Bielsko-Biala, Poland; Department of Ep…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: and objectivesObstructive sleep apnea is significantly underdiagnosed in women, partly because existing screening tools were developed in male-predominant cohorts and may fail to capture female-specific clinical presentations. METHODS: We used the HypnoLaus population-based cohort (n = 1540; 718 women, 822 men) to evaluate seven OSA screening tools in this cross-sectional study and assessed whether adding menopausal status to SARA enhances diagnostic accuracy. Moderate-to-severe OSA was defined as AHI ≥ 15 events per hour on polysomnography. RESULTS: The study included 1540 participants (718 women, 822 men). NoSAS and the updated SARA demonstrated the highest overall discriminative performance, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs), 0.741 (95% CI, 0.718-0.764) and 0.693 (95% CI, 0.669-0.716), respectively, followed by original SARA (AUC, 0.684), Berlin (0.635), SONA (0.579), STOP-Bang (0.575), and ESS (0.507). Incorporation of menopausal status improved discrimination of SARA in women (AUC 0.675 vs. 0.627; p = 0.001). Although NoSAS showed the highest overall AUC, updated SARA performed more consistently across sex-, age-, and BMI-defined phenotypes. In women ≤55 years, updated SARA showed higher discrimination than NoSAS (AUC 0.616 vs. 0.509; p = 0.014), and in lean women (BMI <25 kg/m2), updated SARA detected cases that NoSAS missed (sensitivity 42.3% vs. 0%). CONCLUSIONS: Sex-related differences affect OSA screening. Incorporating menopausal status into SARA improved OSA detection in women. At the same time, anthropometry-weighted tools such as NoSAS performed poorly in younger, leaner women, underscoring the limitations of anthropometry-based screening in these phenotypes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Fatigue is prevalent and disabling in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but the factors examined and their reported associations vary across studies. OBJECTIVE: To map factors examined in relation to fatigue in COPD, characterize their reported association patterns, and descriptively group factors with verifiable direct associations according to potential amenability to change or potential relevance to clinical management. METHODS: This PRISMA-ScR-guided review searched Embase, Scopus, and MEDLINE from inception to 30 April 2026. Eligible primary quantitative studies involved adults with COPD and examined at least one distinct factor in relation to a fatigue outcome or explicit fatigue-specific domain. Layer 1 mapped factor-specific fatigue analyses and classified reported findings as significant, non-significant, mixed/attenuated, or not ascertainable. Layer 2 descriptively organized factors with at least one verifiable statistically significant direct association into author-defined categories of potential amenability to change or potential relevance to clinical management. Frequencies were calculated at the publication level. RESULTS: Thirty-eight publications were included; evidence was predominantly observational and cross-sectional. In Layer 1, dyspnea (24 publications), lung function impairment (17), depressive symptoms (15), and anxiety symptoms (10) were frequently mapped. Factors grouped by potential amenability to change included depressive symptoms (11 publications), anxiety symptoms (6), sleep disturbance (6), smoking status (4), exercise capacity (4), and BMI/body composition (2). Factors grouped by potential relevance to clinical management included dyspnea (20), pain (4), comorbidity status/burden (2), current exacerbation (2), and cough (2). CONCLUSION: Fatigue-related factors in COPD span multiple domains. Dyspnea was prominent among factors potentially relevant to clinical management, whereas depressive and anxiety symptoms, sleep disturbance, smoking status, and exercise capacity were prominent among potentially change-oriented factors. These descriptive findings inform future research but do not establish causality or clinical priority.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) are a leading cause of hospitalisation and mortality. Although multidisciplinary team (MDT) care models are increasingly used in disease management, long-term real-world data, particularly during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of patients hospitalised for AECOPD between 2018 and 2024. A LINE-based MDT model was implemented in 2019. Outcomes included pharmacological and nonpharmacological intervention rates, psychological well-being, health-related quality of life (HRQL), hospital length of stay (LOS), readmissions, and 1-year survival. RESULTS: Among 568 patients, the use of several guideline-based treatments differed significantly across study years, including long-acting muscarinic antagonists (64% in 2018 to 93% in 2024), long-acting beta-agonists (74% to 100%), systemic corticosteroids (79% to 96%), and inhaled corticosteroids (59% to 86%) (all p<0.001). Pulmonary rehabilitation differed significantly across years (p<0.001), increasing from 51.9% in 2018 to 98.6% in 2024 despite a temporary decline in 2022. Smoking cessation success also differed across years (p=0.006). The 14-day readmission rate differed significantly across years (p=0.043), ranging from a peak of 17.3% in 2020 to 2.9% in 2024. No significant differences across years were observed in LOS or 1-year survival. Psychological distress and CAT scores also differed across study years. CONCLUSION: The LINE-based MDT model was associated with higher rates of several care-process measures, particularly pulmonary rehabilitation. However, adjusted comparisons between 2024 and 2018 showed no significant differences in major hospital outcomes. These observational findings suggest a potential role for digitally coordinated MDT care in supporting multidisciplinary AECOPD care, although causal effects cannot be established. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Whether house dust mite sublingual immunotherapy (HDM-SLIT) provides additional clinical benefits in patients with severe asthma already controlled by biologic therapy remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effects of add-on HDM-SLIT on rhinitis-related and asthma-related outcomes in patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma and allergic rhinitis. METHODS: In this propensity score-matched real-world study, 86 patients with severe asthma and allergic rhinitis were analyzed after 1:1 matching of patients receiving HDM-SLIT with those receiving biologic therapy or continuing biologic therapy alone (43 patients per group). Changes in Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (RQLQ), Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire (AQLQ), Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ)-6, lung function, type 2 biomarkers, and airway structural parameters by quantitative computed tomography were evaluated over 12 months. Covariate-adjusted analyses and a sensitivity analysis restricted to patients receiving dupilumab were performed. RESULTS: RQLQ showed greater improvement with HDM-SLIT than with control (standardized mean differences [SMD] 1.545, 95% CI 0.910-2.180; p <0.001), and this finding remained significant in covariate-adjusted and dupilumab-restricted sensitivity analyses. AQLQ also improved with HDM-SLIT (SMD 0.673, 95% CI 0.097-1.250; p = 0.036). ACQ-6, FEV1% predicted, and percentage of airway wall area relative to total area (WA/Ao%) showed nominally greater improvements in the primary analyses (p = 0.023, 0.039, and 0.038, respectively). but these findings were not statistically significant after additional covariate adjustment. CONCLUSION: In patients with biologic-controlled severe asthma with allergic rhinitis, the most consistent benefit associated with add-on HDM-SLIT was improvement in rhinitis-related quality of life.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mechanical power describes the rate of mechanical energy transfer to the respiratory system but does not directly quantify injurious tissue dissipation. In severe left-right asymmetry, global airway-opening values may conceal major differences in lung-specific mechanics. Uniform settings may overdistend the more compliant lung while inadequately ventilating the affected lung. MAIN TEXT: This physiology-driven narrative review examines independent lung ventilation (ILV) for applying lung-specific ventilatory goals and mechanical constraints in severe left-right asymmetry. ILV may be considered when conventional ventilator optimization is ineffective or poorly tolerated and shared settings impose incompatible requirements. Implementation requires anatomical and circuit separation and may involve double-lumen tubes, bronchial blockers in selected configurations, two ventilators, or differential-ventilation systems. A proposed physiological framework aims to limit excessive tidal expansion and pressure exposure in the more compliant lung while adapting ventilation of the affected lung to recruitability, time-constant abnormalities, or air-leak physiology. Lung-specific estimates of delivered mechanical power may characterize mechanical loading but do not directly measure injurious tissue dissipation. Evidence remains limited, deriving from physiological studies, technical reports, and case-based clinical experience. CONCLUSION: In severe left-right asymmetry, global mechanical power may obscure differences in lung-specific mechanical conditions. ILV may permit individualized ventilation when shared settings impose incompatible requirements, but redistribution or reduction of delivered energy alone does not establish lung protection. Whether appropriately selected ILV settings reduce injurious regional mechanical processes, ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI), or adverse clinical outcomes remains to be determined.

papers.abstract_en: Efferocytosis is essential for tissue homeostasis and resolution of inflammation, yet its direct contribution to resolve organ fibrosis remains poorly understood. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive age-driven lung disease, we found profound suppression of efferocytosis coupled with robust production and release of extracellular vesicles presenting functional receptor CD47, a canonical "don't eat me" mediator. Restoration of efferocytosis contributes to the natural resolution of fibrosis, which is accelerated by CD47 deficiency or alterations in macrophage metabolic responses. In turn, pharmacologic disruption of efferocytic receptors or signaling results in lung fibrosis development and its persistence. While sustained reduction of efferocytic capacity align with fibrosis persistence in aged mice, AMPK activation promotes fibrosis resolution via reducing inflammaging and CD47 bioavailability, thus restoring clearance of apoptotic fibroblast. Importantly, AMPK activation also reprograms macrophages engaging apoptotic fibroblasts toward a fibrosis pro-resolving phenotype by suppressing TGF-β1 and promoting secretion of pro-regenerative hepatocyte growth factor (HGF). Together, these findings link metabolism and immune efferocytic fitness in lung fibrosis resolution and suggest that an AMPK senomorphic pathway has broad therapeutic relevance for fibrotic diseases.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Reactive oxygen species are increased across most pulmonary hypertension (PH) etiologies, resulting in increased reactive lipid dicarbonyls, which form protein adducts and impair mitochondrial function. We hypothesized that reducing reactive lipids would reduce right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP) and improve cardiac function by eliminating protein-lipid damage feedback loops. METHODS: We used 2-hydroxybenzylamine (2-HOBA) to scavenge reactive lipids in three complimentary mouse models of PH: AKR-high fat diet (HFD, metabolic stress), LNAME-HFD (cardiometabolic syndrome), and pulmonary artery banding (PAB, load stress). Cardiac function was measured by echocardiography and catheterization. RV energy metabolism was determined by oxygraphy. Mass spectrometry analyzed lipids and ceramides; O-link and RNA-Seq evaluated proteomic and gene expression in lungs, RV, and LV. RESULTS: Reducing reactive lipids with 2-HOBA resulted in a ~ 10% reduction in RVSP, reduced diastolic dysfunction, reduced plasma lipids and ceramides, and normalized RV fatty acid oxidation that was severely impaired in the AKR-HFD and PAB models. Proteomic and RNA changes in the lungs, RV, and LV suggested reduced oxidative damage and inflammatory signaling and altered developmental and actin organization signaling; these changes are plausibly associated with the improved adaptation. Some changes were sex specific, including a 4x higher cardiac fatty acid content in males than females. CONCLUSIONS: Reactive lipid scavenging improves cardiac metabolic and diastolic function and right ventricular systolic pressure through restoration of mitochondrial function and reduced oxidative protein damage. The magnitude of hemodynamic improvement combined with substantial diastolic function improvement suggests clinical potential, particularly for PH patients with metabolic comorbidities.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are well recognized, but their association with dynamic upper airway collapse remains poorly characterized. OBJECTIVE: To characterize sex-related clinical profiles in OSA through the integrated assessment of clinical characteristics, sleep study parameters, and drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) findings. METHODS: This retrospective study compared clinical profiles, sleep parameters, collapse patterns, airway reversibility, and treatment recommendations in 767 patients undergoing DISE. RESULTS: Women were older and more frequently reported insomnia and mood disorders, whereas men had higher body mass index, larger tonsils, and higher Mallampati scores. Sleep study differences were also observed: men exhibited longer apneas, higher apnea-to-hypopnea ratios, and more positional OSA. Respiratory event clustering suggestive of REM-related OSA was more frequent in women, although REM sleep was not EEG-confirmed. DISE demonstrated that obstruction was more frequent in men at all assessed levels, including palatal concentric collapse (62.5% vs 40.7%). Complete resolution with jaw thrust was more frequent in women (30.2% vs 18.4%). Mandibular advancement therapy was more commonly recommended for women, whereas surgery was more frequently recommended for men. CONCLUSIONS: Findings in this DISE-selected cohort suggest a predominantly anatomy-driven pattern in men and a potentially more functionally modulated profile in women, supporting the integration of sex-related characteristics into personalized treatment selection.

papers.abstract_en: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by recurrent alveolar epithelial injury, maladaptive repair, fibroblast activation, and extracellular-matrix accumulation. Lactate metabolism is increasingly implicated in communication between stromal and immune cells in fibrotic lung niches through monocarboxylate transporter (MCT)-mediated transport, hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 1 (HCAR1/GPR81) sensing, extracellular acidification, and lysine lactylation. This narrative review evaluates the evidence for directional lactate-associated fibroblast-macrophage signaling, the limits of proposed reciprocal interactions, and their therapeutic implications. Human IPF observations, experimental pulmonary-fibrosis studies, and indirect evidence from other disease contexts are separated according to disease relevance and causal resolution. The strongest direct mechanistic evidence supports lactate released by activated myofibroblasts as a stimulus for macrophage histone lactylation and profibrotic transcription, whereas reciprocal macrophage-to-fibroblast lactate feedback remains unproven. Among the lactate-associated targets reviewed, fibroblast-associated MCT4 currently has the most developed preclinical evidence package, supported by disease-relevant observations, target perturbation, and antifibrotic activity in experimental models. However, no lactate-directed therapeutic strategy has yet demonstrated clinical efficacy in IPF. HCAR1/GPR81, lactate-production pathways, and lactylation-associated machinery remain mechanistically compelling but are at earlier stages of pharmacological validation. Overall, available evidence is more consistent with lactate functioning as a context-dependent amplifier or maintenance signal than with a demonstrated uniform initiating role in IPF. Lactate-directed interventions may therefore be considered adjunctive strategies alongside established antifibrotic therapy. Further translation will require cell- and disease-stage-specific causal validation, lesion-resolved target engagement, efficacy in established fibrosis, and a therapeutic window that preserves physiological lactate metabolism.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is frequently complicated by pulmonary hypertension (IPF-PH), a severe condition that worsens symptoms, reduces exercise capacity, and shortens survival. Current anti-fibrotic and PH-targeted therapies show limited efficacy in IPF-PH, and the therapeutic role of tacrolimus in this composite disease remains underexplored. METHODS: A bleomycin-induced IPF-PH rat model was established. Rats were randomized into control, bleomycin model, treprostinil (positive control), and tacrolimus (0.05 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous, 21 days) groups. Right ventricular systolic pressure (RVSP), echocardiography, right ventricular and lung histology, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were assessed. In vitro, C166 endothelial cells and primary rat pulmonary arterial endothelial cells were stimulated with bleomycin with or without tacrolimus; MOVAS smooth muscle cells were stimulated with TGF-β1 with or without tacrolimus. Endpoints included cell viability, tube formation, ROS, SOD/GSH, apoptosis, proliferation/migration, and MAPK/PI3K/AKT signaling. RESULTS: Tacrolimus reduced RVSP, improved PAT/PET and right heart function, attenuated right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary fibrosis, and decreased vascular wall thickness and α-SMA expression. It also downregulated fibrosis markers Fn1 and Col1a1. In endothelial cells, tacrolimus restored P-VEGFR2/VEGFR2 and VE-cadherin expression, promoted tube formation, reduced apoptosis (Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-9/3), and alleviated oxidative stress (ROS, SOD/GSH, Keap1/HO-1). In smooth muscle cells, tacrolimus inhibited TGF-β1-induced proliferation and migration and reduced Ki67 expression. Mechanistically, tacrolimus suppressed MAPK (JNK, ERK, p38) and PI3K/AKT pathway activation in vivo and in vitro. DISCUSSION: Tacrolimus ameliorates bleomycin-induced IPF-PH through vascular remodeling-oriented, multi-target effects, including endothelial protection, suppression of oxidative stress and apoptosis, and inhibition of smooth muscle proliferation, partly via MAPK and PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings support tacrolimus as a potential therapeutic candidate for IPF-PH, especially in patients with prominent vascular remodeling, while highlighting the need for further dose-response, target-specific, immunomodulatory, and delivery optimization studies before clinical translation.

papers.abstract_en: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening inflammatory lung disorder characterized by excessive neutrophilic inflammation and increased microvascular permeability. We previously demonstrated the involvement of the Gq-coupled P2Y2 purinergic receptor (P2RY2) in ARDS pathogenesis. Here, we investigated the contribution of the related purinergic receptor P2Y6 (P2RY6) and defined its cell-type-specific functions using a preclinical mouse model of ARDS. Wild-type female mice were treated with the selective P2RY6 antagonist MRS2578 through intratracheal administration using prophylactic and therapeutic approaches, followed by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) challenge. The role of P2RY6 was further evaluated in global P2ry6 -deficient mice and conditional knockout models targeting specific cellular compartments. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples were analyzed by flow cytometry and multiplex cytokine assays, and lung tissues were assessed by histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Pharmacological inhibition of P2RY6 significantly reduced Ly6G+F4/80⁻ neutrophil accumulation, vascular leakage and pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine production in the ARDS model. Consistently, P2ry6 -deficient mice exhibited reduced Ly6G+F4/80⁻ neutrophil recruitment and attenuated inflammatory responses following LPS challenge. Cell-type-specific deletion revealed that P2RY6 deficiency in Vav-expressing hematopoietic cells and CD11c-expressing cells reproduced the protective phenotype observed in global P2ry6 knockout mice. In contrast, P2RY6 deletion in CD4+ T cells, Scgb1a1-expressing airway epithelial cells or LysM-expressing myeloid cells did not significantly alter ARDS-associated inflammation. Collectively, our findings identify CD11c-expressing P2RY6 + cells as critical regulators of ARDS pathogenesis and highlight P2RY6 as a potential therapeutic target for controlling inflammatory lung injury.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common and devastating complication of advanced malignancies, particularly lung cancer, with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and cytokine therapies have shown promise in solid tumors but are constrained by dose-dependent toxicity and limited efficacy in the pleural cavity. Engineered Mycobacterium smegmatis (M. smegmatis) co-expressing a PD-L1 inhibitor and interleukin-15 immunocytokine (Ms-PI15) represents a novel in situ vaccine platform capable of sustained local drug delivery with favorable biosafety profiles. Here, we investigated the therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms of intrapleural Ms-PI15 administration in a murine MPE model. METHODS: A syngeneic MPE mouse model was established by intrapleural inoculation of luciferase-expressing Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC-Luc) cells into C57BL/6 mice. Mice were treated with intrapleural injections of PBS, Ms-vector (empty vector control), or Ms-PI15. Tumor burden was monitored by bioluminescence imaging. Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of Ms-PI15 were evaluated using DIR fluorescence imaging and bacterial colony enumeration. Flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry were employed to characterize immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment, spleen, and thoracic draining lymph nodes (TDLNs). Biosafety was assessed by histopathological examination and serum biochemistry. RESULTS: Intrapleural administration of Ms-PI15 significantly suppressed MPE development and pleural tumor growth compared with PBS and Ms-vector controls. DIR fluorescence imaging and CFU enumeration demonstrated that Ms-PI15 accumulated predominantly in the pleural tumor microenvironment and TDLNs, peaking at 72 h post-administration, with minimal dissemination to distant organs. Mechanistically, Ms-PI15 remodeled the immune microenvironment by promoting maturation of CD80+CD86+ myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs), driving M1 polarization of tumor-associated macrophages (increased CD86+, decreased CD206+), and significantly enhancing infiltration of CD8 T cells and NK1.1+ NK cells in the pleural tumor, spleen, and TDLNs. No significant histopathological abnormalities or serum biochemical alterations were observed in major organs following Ms-PI15 treatment, confirming its favorable biosafety profile. CONCLUSION: Intrapleural administration of the engineered M. smegmatis Ms-PI15 effectively inhibits MPE progression by remodeling the pleural immune microenvironment toward an antitumor phenotype, while maintaining excellent biosafety. These findings provide a preclinical foundation for the development of intracavitary bacterial immunotherapy as a novel treatment strategy for malignant pleural effusion.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary infections caused by P. aeruginosa (PA) remain a major clinical challenge due to biofilm formation, intrinsic resistance, and limited antibiotic penetration into lung tissues following systemic administration. Imipenem (IPM), a broad-spectrum carbapenem, requires high intravenous doses (500 mg every 6 h with cilastatin) to achieve therapeutic lung levels, leading to frequent dosing and systemic toxicity. Pulmonary delivery via dry powder for inhalation (DPI) offers a targeted alternative. However, formulation development is hindered by the chemical instability, specifically its susceptibility to thermal and hydrolytic degradation in the amorphous state. In this study, a high-dose, chemically stable IPM dry powder for inhalation (IPM-DPI) was developed by co-spray-drying IPM with L-leucine. The optimized 50:50 (w/w) IPM: L-leucine powder exhibited an initial IPM potency of ∼94% and low residual moisture content (<2% w/w). Differential scanning calorimetry and powder X-ray diffraction of IPM-DPI confirmed amorphous IPM and semi-crystalline L-leucine, while Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested intermolecular interactions between IPM and L-leucine. The IPM-DPI demonstrated excellent aerosolization, achieving fine particle fractions of ∼67% (Orbital™ DPI) and ∼53% (RS01® DPI), with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 2.4-3.2 µm and retained antimicrobial potency (minimum inhibitory concentration of 0.125-0.25 µg/mL). IPM-DPI maintained >95% of its initial IPM potency after 6 months at -20 °C, demonstrating improved stability associated with intermolecular interactions between leucine and IMP, with the semi-crystalline leucine phase forming a matrix around IMP molecules within the particle core. Overall, the developed IPM-DPI enables localized pulmonary delivery of imipenem, potentially eliminating the need for cilastatin and reducing systemic toxicity associated with parenteral therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy has reshaped the treatment landscape for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet critical gaps remain in real-time monitoring and personalized adaptation. METHODS: In this observational study, patients were evaluated via imaging and multidisciplinary review for subsequent surgery or radiotherapy after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Serial plasma samples for circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) dynamics and mutational analyses were collected. The endpoint was event-free survival (EFS). A pognostic mutational signature was developed using the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. RESULTS: Among the 138 patients, 46.4% and 52.2% underwent surgery and radiotherapy, respectively. Compared to patients with persistently positive ctDNA, the ctDNA non-shedder exhibited a numerically longer EFS (hazard ratio [HR] 0.26, 95% CI: 0.06-1.25, p = 0.062), and the clearance group exhibited a statistically longer EFS (HR 0.33, 95% CI: 0.11-0.97, p = 0.040).
