papers.abstract_en: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) exposes tissues to recurrent intermittent hypoxia (IH) and is associated with multisystem morbidity. Growing evidence implicates the gut microbiota and microbial metabolism in these consequences, but their contribution to target-organ injury remains uncertain. This narrative review examines how IH remodels the intestinal environment and evaluates the evidence linking these changes to systemic injury, distinguishing preclinical experimental findings from human clinical observations. IH can disturb intestinal oxygen homeostasis, impair epithelial barrier function, and alter microbial and host-microbial metabolic pathways involving short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and trimethylamine N-oxide. These changes may influence distant tissues through metabolic signaling and immune activation. Preclinical studies support a functional microbial contribution to selected cardiovascular, metabolic, and neurocognitive phenotypes, but mechanistic resolution and applicability vary with exposure conditions, diet, and host background. Human studies remain predominantly observational and do not establish microbial mediation of OSA-related organ injury. Overall, the gut microbiota is best regarded as a context-dependent contributor and amplifier of IH-related injury, rather than a universal mediator. A focus on microbial function and host-microbial co-metabolism may be more informative than inconsistent taxonomic signatures. Longitudinal studies and targeted interventions are needed to establish clinical relevance and determine whether microbiome-directed approaches can complement established OSA treatment.

papers.authors: Hu S, Li X, Batool Z, Zheng X, Dong J, Zhang C, Yang Y, Shen B et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine and Institutes for Systems Genetics, Frontiers Science Center for D…
papers.abstract_en: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, remains a major global health challenge, further exacerbated by the rapid emergence of drug-resistant strains. Despite continuous efforts, the discovery of novel anti-TB agents has lagged behind the evolution of resistance, largely due to the limitations of conventional experimental pipelines and the growing biological complexity of the pathogen. In recent years, computational drug discovery approaches-including virtual screening, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven modeling, and hybrid computational frameworks-have substantially expanded the chemical space accessible for early-stage anti-TB research. However, their translational success remains limited. This discrepancy reflects a fundamental mismatch between target-centric computational paradigms and the multi-scale biological constraints of Mtb, including permeability barriers, efflux mechanisms, metabolic state heterogeneity, lesion-level pharmacokinetics, and regimen-dependent therapeutic effects. This review critically evaluates current computational strategies for anti-TB drug screening, with particular emphasis on their performance under TB-specific biological and resistance constraints. We further explore computational approaches designed to address drug-resistant Mtb, including resistance-aware compound design, host-directed therapy, and combination regimen modeling. Finally, we explore key limitations in current computational pipelines, including challenges in data quality, biological integration, and regimen-level modeling, and propose a shift toward biologically grounded, regimen-aware, and systems-level frameworks. Bridging the gap between in silico prediction and clinical efficacy will require integrating multi-scale biological realism into computational pipelines, enabling more reliable translation of computational advances into effective anti-TB therapeutics.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Microbiology, Institute for Viral Diseases, Korea University College of Medicine, Seoul, Republic of Korea…
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Influenza A(H3N2) has resurged in South Korea despite a shrinking pediatric population and high vaccination coverage. We examined correlates of host-age state transitions on the H3N2 hemagglutinin (HA) genealogy. METHODS: We analyzed 703 South Korean H3N2 HA sequences (2009-2025) in eight host-age states (ages 0-4, 5-9, then 10-year bands to 60 years and older). Discrete-trait analysis and an epoch-structured hierarchical generalized linear model (GLM) were fitted over 1700 HA trees, with epochs split at mid-2020. Within-year age-label permutation provided the sampling control (one for the discrete-trait analysis, 20 for the GLM). RESULTS: Children aged 5-9 years showed the largest net source balance (+11.7 vs. +10.5 under permuted labels), reflecting a lower recipient-side rate (0.39 vs. 1.08) rather than a higher source-side rate (12.11 vs. 11.59). Of 56 routes, 18 were supported (Bayes factor ≥ 10) but only three exceeded the permutation control, two from this group. Observed labels fitted the genealogy 400 log-likelihood units better, with 24% fewer transitions. Source-group population size (posterior inclusion probability, 0.74) and vaccination coverage (0.66) were supported, both with negative coefficients; contact rate was not (0.016). Only population size exceeded the permutation null (0.74 vs. 0.65; p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: H3N2 HA lineage transitions in South Korea were age-structured after accounting for sampling, most clearly for children aged 5-9 years. Their net source balance reflects a low recipient-side rate rather than a high source-side rate, and therefore describes lineage position rather than transmission intensity. These findings support age-resolved genomic surveillance for interpreting such patterns.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial structural and functional dysfunction in airway epithelial cells is recognized as a central driver in the progression of severe asthma. However, the current understanding of the mechanisms underlying damage to the mitochondria remains insufficient, and effective therapeutic strategies for its repair are lacking. Fumarate hydratase (FH) is a pivotal metabolic enzyme in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. It exhibits anti-inflammatory and tissue-repairing effects in immune-related diseases, but its contribution to asthma has not been previously reported. METHODS: We examined the role of FH in severe asthma utilizing human transcriptomic datasets and in vitro (airway epithelial cells) and in vivo (mouse) models induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in combination with house dust mites (HDM), in conjunction with FH overexpression and pharmacological inhibition interventions. Mitochondrial function, mitochondrial dynamics, and inflammatory responses were assessed, together with Drp1 overexpression rescue and NRF2 inhibition experiments. RESULTS: Analysis of human severe asthma datasets, together with HDM/LPS-induced cellular and mouse models, consistently revealed reduced FH expression. Restoration of FH expression improved mitochondrial function, suppressed Drp1-associated mitochondrial fission, and reduced airway inflammation, whereas Drp1 overexpression partially reversed the mitochondrial protective effects of FH. FH also reduced Keap1 expression, promoted NRF2 nuclear translocation and HO-1 expression, and NRF2 inhibition attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of FH. CONCLUSION: These findings identify FH as a previously unrecognized metabolic regulator with protective effects in airway inflammation and support a role for mitochondrial fission-fusion dynamics in FH-mediated protection of airway epithelial cells.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by excessive proliferation and migration of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs), yet how hypoxia-associated metabolic reprogramming contributes to pulmonary vascular remodeling remains unclear. Here, we show that hypoxia elevates intracellular lactate in PASMCs, promoting HBO1 (lysine acetyltransferase 7/KAT7)-catalyzed H3K9 lactylation (H3K9la) at the EHMT2 promoter and enhancing EHMT2 transcription. Smooth muscle cell-specific Ehmt2 deletion attenuates pulmonary vascular remodeling and right ventricular hypertrophy in SU5416/hypoxia (SuHx) mice and suppresses PASMC proliferation and migration. Conversely, EHMT2 overexpression promotes these phenotypes and mediates lactate-induced PASMC dysfunction. RNA sequencing of pulmonary arteries from Ehmt2-deficient mice identifies PPARγ repression as a downstream mechanism. Collectively, these findings identify a lactate-H3K9la-EHMT2-PPARγ axis linking hypoxia-induced metabolic reprogramming to pulmonary vascular remodeling and PAH progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) complicated by sepsis remains a life-threatening infectious syndrome associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Although β-lactam-based combination therapy is widely recommended for severe CAP, the optimal empirical antibiotic strategy for septic pneumonia remains uncertain. At the same time, empirical antibiotic selection must balance adequate early treatment against unnecessary broad-spectrum antibiotic use and the risk of antimicrobial resistance. Evidence specifically targeting this high-risk population is limited. This study aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of β-lactam monotherapy and β-lactam-based combination therapy in patients with CAP-associated sepsis. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at Zhejiang Xiaoshan Hospital from January 2021 to January 2025, including adult patients with CAP-associated sepsis who received empirical β-lactam monotherapy or β-lactam-based combination therapy with macrolides or doxycycline within 48 hours of admission. A total of 100 patients were included before propensity score matching, and 80 patients remained after 1:1 matching. The primary outcome was time to clinical stability (TTCS). Secondary outcomes included mortality, length of hospital stay, antibiotic duration, changes in SOFA score, inflammatory biomarkers, clinical cure, and adverse events. TTCS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. RESULTS: Median TTCS was 5.0 days with monotherapy and 4.0 days with combination therapy (P = 0.129). Combination therapy also showed favorable trends in hospitalization duration, clinical cure, inflammatory marker reduction, and organ function recovery. After adjustment for admission SOFA score, combination therapy showed a nonsignificant trend toward earlier clinical stability (adjusted HR 1.42, 95% CI 0.88-2.29; P = 0.151). No significant increase in adverse events was observed. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CAP-associated sepsis, β-lactam-based combination therapy showed a trend toward earlier clinical stability than β-lactam monotherapy, although the difference was not statistically significant. This study addresses an important evidence gap in septic pneumonia management and supports further investigation of individualized antimicrobial strategies guided by disease severity and biological characteristics. The retrospective single-center design and relatively small sample size should be considered when interpreting these findings.

papers.abstract_en: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remains a leading cause of global mortality, driven by declining lung function and frequent exacerbations. Conventional pulmonary rehabilitation (PR) programs usually last 6-12 weeks, and evidence supporting long-term PR is limited. In addition, the role of negative-pressure ventilation (NPV) in the management of COPD remains unclear.ObjectivesThis study investigated the clinical efficacy of a sequential long-term NPV and PR program in patients with COPD.DesignA retrospective cohort study.MethodsWe analyzed 125 COPD patients treated between 2019 and 2023. The intervention group received 12 months of NPV preceding hospital-based PR with lower-limb exercise twice weekly (NPV-PR), while the comparison group received PR alone. Longitudinal outcomes included pulmonary function tests, 6-min walking distance (6-MWD), COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score, Modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea score, and the number of acute exacerbations.ResultsThe NPV-PR group showed significant within-group improvements in pulmonary function, marked by an increased change in forced vital capacity (ΔFVC%) and a significant reduction in residual volume (ΔRV). Despite a lower baseline 6-MWD, the NPV-PR cohort achieved 12-month walking distances comparable to the PR-alone group. Furthermore, CAT scores declined rapidly by 6 months in the NPV-PR group, suggesting NPV may accelerate symptom relief. Notably, the combined approach sustained long-term rehabilitation benefits, yielding significant reductions in mMRC dyspnea scores and the expected count of acute exacerbations.ConclusionOur findings suggest that integrating long-term NPV with extended PR may represent a novel strategy, potentially optimizing the long-term management and clinical trajectory of patients with symptomatic COPD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bronchial asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease and a major global public health concern. Although numerous studies have reported asthma prevalence, evidence focusing specifically on adult populations in Saudi Arabia remains limited and fragmented. This study aimed to systematically review available evidence and estimate the pooled prevalence of bronchial asthma among adults in Saudi Arabia. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar) were searched for studies published between 2010 and 2025. Observational studies reporting asthma prevalence among adults (≥ 18 years) in Saudi Arabia were included. Study selection involved title and abstract screening followed by full-text assessment. Data were extracted using a standardized form, and methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. A random-effects meta-analysis with Freeman-Tukey transformation was performed using JASP software. RESULTS: A total of 1,280 records were identified, of which twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. All included studies were cross-sectional and conducted across national and regional settings. The pooled prevalence of bronchial asthma among adults in Saudi Arabia was 12.9% (95% CI: 8.8%-17.6%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 99.1%, p < 0.001). Prevalence estimates varied widely across studies due to differences in study design, sampling strategies, and asthma definitions. CONCLUSION: Bronchial asthma represents a significant public health burden among adults in Saudi Arabia. The high heterogeneity highlights the need for standardized epidemiological methods and improved surveillance. Strengthening prevention, early diagnosis, and disease management strategies is essential to reduce the burden of asthma and improve population health outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a life-threatening disease driven by progressive pulmonary vascular remodeling, and aberrant phenotypic transition of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) serves as the core pathological driver of disease deterioration. Sinomenine (SIN), a structurally defined isoquinoline alkaloid isolated from Sinomenium acutum (Thunb.) Rehder & E.H.Wilson, exhibits anti-inflammatory, vascular-protective, and anti-remodeling activities. Nevertheless, the exact molecular mechanism by which SIN regulates PASMC dysfunction to prevent PAH remains unclear. In vivo, SIN administration significantly attenuated MCT-induced PAH, right ventricular hypertrophy and pulmonary vascular remodeling in rats. In vitro, SIN effectively suppressed platelet-derived growth factor-BB (PDGF-BB)-triggered proliferation, migration and phenotypic switching of PASMCs. RNA-sequencing coupled with KEGG enrichment analysis further identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the key signaling cascade dysregulated by MCT, with osteopontin (OPN) validated as the central functional target of SIN. OPN overexpression recapitulated the pro-remodeling effects of PDGF-BB in PASMCs, and such abnormal phenotypes were prevented by SIN. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay demonstrated that SIN binds to NF-κB, a transcription factor of OPN, and suppresses PDGF-BB-induced NF-κB activation. This study uncovers a novel mechanism of SIN against PAH and highlights OPN as a critical mediator of its protective effects.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Anti-tuberculosis drug resistance has become a major challenge to global tuberculosis control. This study aims to comprehensively the global burden, trends, and risks for disease deaths of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB), extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB), HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB from 1990 to 2021. METHODS: Data on the incidence and deaths of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB were obtained from GBD 2021. The estimated annual percentage change (EAPC) and fold change were calculated to assess the trends of disease burden changes from baseline (1990 for MDR-TB and HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB; 1993 for XDR-TB and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB) to 2021. RESULTS: In 2021, the highest age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) and age-standardized death rates (ASDR) were observed in MDR-TB globally, with 5.4161 (3.1676-9.3429) and 1.2791 (0.4992-2.5331) per 100,000 population, respectively. A significant increase in the global incidence and death burden of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has been reported from baseline to 2021. Especially for HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB, death cases increased 84.89-fold, with an EAPC in ASDR of 10 (6.26-13.86). In contrast, MDR-TB demonstrated a comparatively smaller increase, with death cases rising 5.65-fold and an EAPC in ASDR of 1.18 (-0.37-2.75). Over the past 32 years, the incidence and death ratio of these types of DR-TB in the High-middle SDI region have been the highest. In terms of age patterns, the burden of MDR-TB and XDR-TB has increased most significantly in the 15-49 age group. In contrast, the burden of HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has notably increased among those aged 5-14. CONCLUSION: Over the past 30 years, a significant increase in the global burden of MDR-TB, XDR-TB, HIV/AIDS-MDR-TB, and HIV/AIDS-XDR-TB has been reported, with marked variations in various resistance types across different regions and countries. In particular, the high-middle SDI regions warrant special attention. These findings highlight the need for further research to identify effective intervention strategies tailored to the epidemiological patterns observed in different regions and populations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer exhibits profound clinical, radiological, and biological heterogeneity, which poses significant challenges for early recognition and timely diagnosis in select atypical cases. Among rare manifestations, massive bronchorrhea caused by EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma with radiological findings of a dominant pulmonary nodule and migratory ground-glass opacities (GGOs) remains extremely uncommon. CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male patient presented with massive bronchorrhea and progressive dyspnea. Serial chest computed tomography (CT) scans revealed bilateral migratory GGOs and a small nodular lesion in the basal segment of the right lower lobe. Empiric antibiotic therapy and subsequent systemic corticosteroid treatment failed to alleviate his respiratory symptoms. Ultimately, markedly elevated sputum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) levels, combined with pathological results from transbronchial biopsy of the right lung nodule, confirmed a diagnosis of EGFR-mutated lung adenocarcinoma. Treatment with osimertinib achieved rapid resolution of bronchorrhea, accompanied by complete regression of the pulmonary nodule and GGOs during clinical follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for lung adenocarcinoma in patients with persistent unexplained bronchorrhea. For patients harboring EGFR-sensitive mutations, EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) remain the first-line treatment, yielding favorable therapeutic effects on bronchorrhea control and improving survival outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Large pedunculated submucosal lesions of the proximal esophagus are uncommon. Their mobility and bulk can obscure the pedicle and restrict safe access for conventional endoscopic resection. We describe a single illustrative case and a rigid endoscopic technique in which a flexible detachable loop is tightened around the lesion, released from its delivery catheter and grasped by its free proximal tail to maintain traction during monopolar resection. A 75-year-old woman with progressive dysphagia had a 15-mm pedunculated lesion in the proximal esophagus. The lesion was excised without a perioperative complication and histology confirmed a submucosal lipoma. Solid food was gradually reintroduced, dysphagia had resolved by 6 months, and there was no clinical evidence of recurrence at 1 year. Snare-assisted suspension may facilitate exposure and manipulation of selected pedunculated benign-appearing esophageal lesions during rigid endoscopy. Further evaluation is required to determine wider applicability and clinical benefit.

papers.abstract_en: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease that affects various tissues of the body. One of these tissues is the lung, in which pleuropulmonary manifestations commonly occur. In these patients, homeostasis is disrupted, characterized by a decrease in Treg and an increase in Th1 and Th2 cells. Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are a cell population characterized by their ability to suppress the T cell response; however, in recent years, the presence of major histocompatibility complex class II (MHC-II) molecules on MDSCs has been reported. Nevertheless, the presence of costimulatory molecules, such as CD80, CD86, and ICOSL, has not been studied yet in MDSCs expressing MHC-II in the context of SLE. In this study, we evaluated the pulmonary microenvironment in SLE mice from an immunological and histological perspective. We observed increased pro-inflammatory cytokines and cellular infiltration in lungs of SLE mice. We also observed MDSC MHC-II cells expressing CD80, CD86, and ICOSL in this tissue, along with alterations of CD4+ T cells subsets, characterized by a decrease in IL-10 frequency in SLE mice. Moreover, we observed that G-MDSCs MHC-II expressing CD80, CD86, or ICOSL correlate positively with phenotypes of CD4+ T cells that produce IL-17 and IFN-γ. For this reason, we suggest that MHC-II+ G-MDSC cells may contribute to an inflammatory environment that triggers tissue damage in the lungs of SLE mice.

papers.abstract_en: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are emerging as critical post-transcriptional regulators that control multiple stages of RNA life cycle, thereby linking post-transcriptional programs to cellular function. Increasing evidence implicates dysregulated RBP-RNA interactions in key pathological mechanisms underlying interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), including epithelial injury, fibroblast activation, immune dysregulation and impaired tissue repair. In idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), cytoplasmic retention of the RBP Fused in Sarcoma (FUS) in patient derived fibroblasts is associated with preferential binding to profibrotic transcripts, while antisense oligonucleotide mediated suppression of FUS attenuates fibrotic signaling and enhances epithelial regenerative programs in cellular, ex vivo and 3D models. Emerging findings across ILD subtypes suggest that RBP dysregulation may represent a broader post-transcriptional phenomenon. Here, we review the principles governing RBP-RNA interactions, approaches for identifying and measuring these interactions and the links between RBPs, aging and lung pathology. We further discuss the emerging role of RBPs as post-transcriptional orchestrators of ILD pathogenesis and consider their potential as therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: RA-ILD is a serious complication of RA. Patients are prone to spontaneous pneumothorax and have a higher risk of lung cancer.Given poor lung function and high risk of pneumothorax recurrence, conventional biopsy is challenging, making diagnosis difficult. CASE PRESENTATION: A 67-year-old male with a history of smoking and well-controlled rheumatoid arthritis presented with chest tightness and pleuritic chest pain. On admission, he was found to have respiratory failure (PaO₂ 58.9mmHg). Chest CT revealed left-sided pneumothorax with interstitial lung disease.Following closed thoracic drainage, the pneumothorax resolved, which was confirmed by follow-up chest X-ray.But the persistence of the patient's chest pain despite resolution of the pneumothorax prompted further investigation.CT pulmonary angiography identified a suspicious mass in the left lower lobe with adjacent rib destruction and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given the high risk of recurrent pneumothorax from percutaneous biopsy in a patient with recent pneumothorax and pre-existing respiratory failure, a multidisciplinary team recommended Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration(EBUS-TBNA) as a safer alternative. EBUS of enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes (stations 7 and 11L) confirmed poorly differentiated lung adenocarcinoma.The patient subsequently received first-line chemotherapy with pemetrexed, cisplatin, and bevacizumab, after which his condition gradually stabilized. CONCLUSION: Both pneumothorax and interstitial lung disease can mask an occult malignancy, underscoring the need for clinical vigilance. EBUS-TBNA is a safe and effective diagnostic option in such high-risk cases.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: More than one billion people live within 100 km of an active volcano, yet the respiratory hazard of ash resists generalization. Bulk composition modulates eruption parameters, therefore respirability, and determines the availability of crystalline silica and labile metals in basaltic ash. AREAS COVERED: We review the health-pertinent properties of volcanic ash, consistently reported symptoms of acute exposure, and the thin, confounded evidence for chronic disease, where co-exposure to volcanic gases and aerosols impairs attribution. We develop an underexplored possibility: volcanic environments increase the risk of environmentally acquired lung infection via ash fomites carrying viable bacteria, innate defense impairment, including iron-dependent nutritional immunity, and selection for pathogen metal-resistance systems in metal-rich volcanic environments. Nontuberculous mycobacterial lung disease in Hawai'i and an exploratory country-level comparison of epidemiology metrics with volcanism test whether the disease axis is visible in existing data. EXPERT OPINION: Volcanic ash hazards are eruption-specific and crystalline silica and labile metals are joined by a scarcely tested third. That is, environmentally acquired bacterial lung infections are higher in 'volcanic' countries and account for a greater share of respiratory infections; both outcomes are ecological and hypothesis-generating. The infectious disease pathway and health effects of chronic exposure remain the least constrained assessment element.

papers.abstract_en: Asthma is a heterogeneous disease characterized by chronic airway inflammation and airway remodeling. Growing evidence suggests that mitochondrial dysfunction is not only a consequence of inflammatory injury but may also contribute to disease persistence and progression. In asthma, mitochondrial redox balance, energy metabolism, Ca2+ homeostasis, dynamics, biogenesis, and quality control can all become dysregulated. These abnormalities are interconnected and can alter mitochondrial energy supply, structural integrity, and quality maintenance. Mitochondrial damage can increase mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, promote the mislocalization of mitochondrial nucleic acids, alter membrane lipid oxidation and remodeling, and induce the release of mitochondrial proteins and other components. These changes generate diverse mitochondria-derived damage signals that can regulate inflammation-related gene transcription, nucleic acid sensing, and inflammasome activation. More broadly, mitochondrial abnormalities also alter immune cell function, airway epithelial repair, smooth muscle cell accumulation, and extracellular matrix production. Together, these effects may contribute to persistent airway inflammation and airway remodeling. This review summarizes the major forms of mitochondrial dysfunction in asthma. It also examines how these abnormalities generate mitochondria-derived damage signals, engage inflammatory sensing, and alter immune and airway structural cell functions.
